b.titles: Best: 'Tell Vera what to plan.' (figure lineage). As the box's label it says who hears you and what to type, and it ends on the lit word where the eye stops. It fits one phone line, and it is the clearest instruction to a field in the tour. A close second is 'What are we planning?' (t2-console-graft). It is an open, household 'we' invitation, and 'planning' covers the whole job, but a question reads a little less plainly as 'type here' than the imperative does. 'What's the plan?' (console-refine, switchboard-refine/mut) is warm and short, but on its own it can read as 'show me the plan', a request for a display rather than an invitation to write. It works on the switchboard only because the prompt caret sits right under it on the glass; in console-refine's box frame it is weaker. 'Anything to plan?' (switchboard-graft) is vague and reads as a yes/no question, and on the phone the date and radar push it down the screen. 'Tell Vera what's next.' (t1-console-graft, console-mut) is too narrow: ideas kept for later and wish lists are not 'next', and 'next' collides with the NEXT UP tube beside it. Today's 'What's on your mind?' fails: it names no job.

b.notes: I looked at every home at full size, the strips, the phone sheet and the details, plus full-size Status, Chat, To do, Plans and Settings for the leaders. The three lineages have each found a figure device worth making the standard: Figure Ground's space-padded tabular rail dates with 'Fig. N' captions, Flight Console's leader readouts (label ····· figure), and the Switchboard graft's leading day numerals. A winner could adopt any of them on every page. The common fault across the heat is leader overuse: dotted leaders across the chat (figure-refine), across 600px plan rows (console-refine) and through every register row (switchboard-graft). A leader should bridge a gap the eye cannot jump, not draw a rule through the reading. Keep them on contents heads and readouts, and cap list measures near 46rem. The second common fault is ids and zero-padding set as if they were content: '#4' ahead of titles, 05/07/01 readouts, 01–04 chat numbers. The refinements that removed them read better every time. VT323 is at its best for short machine lines on the glass (Next up, countdowns, 'Anything to plan?') and worst on any line with an apostrophe. Grafts: margin-numbered chat (figure-graft) worked and should replace refine's leaders. Day numerals shared with the radar (switchboard-graft) worked and are the best new idea. The folded empty weeks as one dim line (figure-graft, console-graft) worked. Dimension ticks around relative dates (figure-graft) hurt the column. The master caution band (console-graft) is a sound component but is typeset too densely on one line. Barlow small caps (console-mut) did not work. Against the yardsticks: t2-figure-refine and t2-console-refine now beat Desk Terminal, Joined (7.0) on typesetting, and every refinement clearly improves on today's page (5.0).

scores.why: The most complete type system in the heat. Named styles sit on a 4px grid (question 52/1.05 condensed, head 28/32, lede 18/28, row 16/24, label 13/20). Rail dates are set in tabular mono and space-padded, so 'Thu  1 Oct' lines up with 'Sat 17 Oct'. Every tracked-caps kind label is now sentence case, 'kids’' has its curly apostrophe, the task ids are gone from Home, 'Then you’re ready.' replaces READY, and 'Fig. 1' captions give it a real manual voice. It loses points on the chat, where ~950px dotted leaders rule across the reading measure.

The leader readouts ('Plans ········ 5', 'Working ········ 5') are one typesetting device used on Home, Status, To do and Ideas, with plain unpadded figures, and it reads as a system. The due column is well set: a sentence line over a mono date line ('Was due 3 days ago / Sun 27 Sep, 19:56'). The title sits cleanly in the box's frame with a true apostrophe. It is let down by ~600px leaders in the Coming up rows, amber '#4' ids in front of the task titles, and a 60px break between the box and its ways to start.

The best new typographic idea in the heat: each plan row is led by a large light calendar numeral (1, 4, 9, 17, 24) with its weekday stacked small beside it, and the same numerals label the radar. 'Anything to plan?' is the one VT323 title with no apostrophe gap. But dotted leaders run through nearly every row on every register, which makes the texture busy, and row 1 crams 'Thu/Oct', a dot and 'Next up' into one small slot.

It has refine's base and grafts in two good things. The chat's margin numbers keep the reading measure clean, where refine's leaders cut across it. Ids now follow the titles in small dim type. It also grafts two bad ones. The dimension ticks around 'in 4 days' break the clean right edge of the relative column and add noise to every row. On To do, 'Edit' drops under the due line.

The title 'What are we planning?' is well set, and the folded 'nothing planned' strip and the kids' wishes sentence read nicely. The master caution band crams five voices onto one line: a bold head, an amber mono '3 steps', a bold underlined link, small 'then…' words and a right-hand link. '3 of 4 on' mixes mono figures with a sans word, and the readout labels stacked over their figures are plainer than refine's leaders.

The bigger VT323 in Next up and the Plans countdown tube is welcome phosphor type. Otherwise it keeps the parent's faults: 12px tracked mono-caps eyebrows (WHO ANSWERS, READY), zero-padded chat numbers (01–04) and '#4' ids in front of titles.

A strong manual base: condensed display heads, captions, and mono tabular dates and times. Still present: tracked mono caps for the kinds (ACTIVITY, RESTAURANT), READY, ids leading the task titles, and a straight apostrophe in 'The kids' wishes'. The refinement fixes all of these.

A tidy condensed and mono pairing, with lamp bars beside tabular times. The zero-padded readouts (05, 04, 02, 03) read as codes, and the title 'Tell Vera what’s next.' is set well but is narrower than the job.

It drops the parent's tracked caps ('After Next up', 'Lately added', 'Who / Due' are now sentence case), and 'Figure + small unit' ('4 open · 2 late') is well proportioned. The two tube strengths on the title are an expressive device. But VT323 gives the apostrophe a full cell ('What ’s'), sky-tinted weekday and month words make a date look like two things, and a setup step wraps to leave 'phones.' as a widow.
The type is the parent's (mono-caps eyebrows, WHO/DUE, VT323 apostrophe gap). The new meters add stacked 'IN 30 DAYS / 6 CALLS' caps but no typographic gain.
A good contents-line grammar (name, leader, figure, unit) and page numbers. But it has many tracked mono-caps labels, the VT323 apostrophe gap in the title, and small boxed setup numerals.

Hanging markers outside the text edge are a real compositor's refinement, but they are applied inconsistently. It now uses four families (Plex, Azeret, Barlow, VT323). Barlow's small caps read as tracked caps again, and Azeret's slashed zeros make the zero-padding (05, 07, 01) louder. That is change that costs legibility.

It is clean and readable, but the hierarchy is flat (heads around 20px, close to the body), with tracked mono eyebrows (WEDNESDAY 30 SEPTEMBER, SOMETHING TO EAT), date blocks with no tabular column, and no figures system.

Mature: condensed heads with numbered rings, right-aligned mono figures and leaders, figure-over-label stacks. It still has tracked mono caps (PLANS, OPEN, WHO, DUE), a VT323 title with the apostrophe gap, and 'in 4 days' letter-spaced in mono.

fixes.suggestion: KEEP: the named type tokens on the 4px grid, the space-padded tabular rail dates, sentence-case kind words, the 'Fig. N' caption style (bold blueprint number, regular caption), the inline subhead 'Next up, then 4 more', and 'Then you’re ready.' FIX the chat: end each speaker's leader at the thread's left gutter rather than running it ~950px to the speaker, or adopt figure-graft's margin numbers and arrows. Either way, no rule should cross a message's measure. FIX the step between Home's 52px question and its 28px plate heads: add a 22px step for Home's plate heads (Coming up, To do, Finish setting up) so the plates rank below the question. FIX the Plans list: stop each row's hairline at the 46rem measure with its facts. FIX To do: set the '#4' after the title at label size in --dim, as figure-graft does, and keep 'Edit' on the due line with a fixed-width due column. Put the rail dates in the chat (the date rule 'Sunday 27 September') in the same mono date style as the other rails.

KEEP: the leader readouts ('Label ····· N', unpadded figures, the one amber tube digit for Late) as the standard figure device on every page; the two-line due cell (sentence over mono date); the title in the box's frame with a curly apostrophe; the leg lengths over the arcs. FIX Coming up: the dotted leaders run ~600px from title to relative date. Either cap the list at ~46rem with the calendar note beside it, as the parent did, or put 'in 4 days' right after the time and drop the leader. FIX To do (Home and the page): move '#4' after the title at small size in dim, not amber ahead of it. Amber should mean late, not id. FIX the 60px pool between the box and the ways to start: close it to 12–16px so they read as one block. FIX the chat's date rule: '27 Sep' should be 'Sun 27 Sep', matching the rails. Set the leg labels in the readout face with tabular figures rather than a separate 12px mono.

KEEP: the leading day numerals (light, large, tabular, right-aligned in a fixed 2ch column) with the weekday stacked small, and the numerals shared with the radar. They are the heat's best new typographic idea and would work on the Plans list and the month too. KEEP 'Anything to plan?' in VT323 at two strengths. FIX the leader overuse: keep leaders on the contents heads (name ····· figure unit) and remove them from list rows (Ideas, To do, Plans), where a column already carries the eye. FIX row 1: take 'Next up' out of the numeral slot. Let the lit numeral mean next, or put 'tomorrow · next' in the relative column. FIX the Settings head plate: its title is smaller than on the other pages; use one --t-title for every plate. FIX the foot strip: align Wishes, Memory, Family, Status and Settings to the three columns above. On the phone, shorten the tube date to 'Wed 30 Sep' so VT323 does not wrap.

KEEP: the margin-number chat, which should replace refine's leaders; ids after titles; the Plans head line 'Next  Silver Falls hike  Thu 1 Oct, 10:00'; the folded '31 Aug – 27 Sep  Nothing on.' strip. DROP the dimension ticks around the relative dates, or at least right-align the words and draw the ticks as a 40% hairline, so the column keeps one clean right edge. FIX To do: 'Edit' wraps under the due words; give the due column a fixed width.

FIX the VT323 apostrophe in 'What’s the plan?': wrap the ’ in a span with negative margins (about -0.3em each side), or use the lineage's 'Anything to plan?'. Set the plan dates' weekday and month in --dim neutral, not sky, so a date reads as one unit. Give the setup list a wider measure or text-wrap: pretty so 'phones.' does not sit alone. Keep the sentence-case column heads and the 'figure + small unit' counts.

Split the master caution band into two lines: a head ('Finish setting up · 3 steps', in sans, not amber mono) and, below it, the next step as the one link, with 'then Telegram, then Google Calendar' after it in dim. Set the '3 of 4 on' counts in the readout face throughout, not mono figures beside a sans word. Carry refine's leader readouts rather than labels stacked over figures.

Carry only the hanging markers (step numerals, lamps and bullets outside the text edge), applied everywhere or nowhere, phone included. Go back to IBM Plex Mono and drop Barlow, the small caps and the zero-padding: four families and slashed-zero padded codes cost more than they give.

Take its larger Next up and Plans countdown VT323 treatment into refine. Drop the 01–04 chat numbers, the 12px tracked mono eyebrows (WHO ANSWERS, READY) and the ids before titles, all of which refine already fixed.

b.titles: Best: 'Tell Vera what to plan.' (Figure Ground). It is an imperative in the manual's voice that names who hears you and states the whole job in one verb. The lit word lands at the end of the line, where the eye stops, and the full stop makes it a sentence rather than a slogan. Set in Plex Sans Condensed 600 it holds one line on a phone at 2rem. Second: 'What’s the plan?' (Flight Console refine, Switchboard refine). It is the family's own kitchen-table phrase and very short, and it sets beautifully in a proportional face with a curly apostrophe (console-refine). In VT323 (switchboard) the apostrophe takes a full monospace cell and reads as 'What ’s', a typesetting fault the family will see on the most prominent line of the page. 'Anything to plan?' (switchboard-graft) is the right choice for a VT323 glass: no apostrophe, friendly, and the lit word is still the job. It does not name Vera, but the glass is hers. 'What are we planning?' (console-graft) has a warm household 'we', but its eight-letter lit word is a large glowing area and the line reads more like a status question than an invitation. It fails least in a proportional face. It fails when… it doesn't; it simply works less well than the two above. 'Tell Vera what’s next.' (console-mut, kept by rule) fails: it narrows the job (ideas for someday and wish lists are not 'next'), and 'next' collides with the NEXT UP label beside it.

b.notes: No design listed a removal (every removed.txt is empty), and every candidate has 0 targets under 44px on every page, so the differences are in wayfinding and in how state reads. Tab order is fixed in every new entrant: the box comes straight after the bar. It is still broken in the carried t1-console-graft, t2-console-mut (seven rail cells first), t1-switchboard-refine and t2-switchboard-mut (three links first). Legibility: t2-figure-refine has the largest minimum type (13-15px); console-refine (4.52), switchboard-refine (4.67) and console-graft (4.64) have the lowest text contrast. Grafted features that worked for the family: the one-line master caution / setup line (console-graft, switchboard-graft), which gives a first-time admin one next step instead of a checklist; plain words beside lamps (console-refine); folding empty past weeks on the month (console-graft, figure-graft); the day numerals leading plan rows (switchboard-graft); the 'Next in 1 day' ring and countdown screen on Plans (figure-graft, figure-mut), readable at a glance. Grafts that cost usability: pencil-hatched kind squares (less distinct than solid swatches, though the word carries them); numbered margin arrows in the chat (clutter on the phone); dimension ticks on 'in 4 days' (decoration the row already says); switchboard-graft's radar numerals (too small at 1x); the switchboard-mut meter's square-root scale (easy to misread). A cross-lineage pattern worth making standard: one notice component (amber edge, what waits, the next step as a link) used on Home, Status and Settings, plus a word beside every lamp. With that, every design here would let a family member tell what state things are in without a legend. Check the Wishes page and the Plans list view in the next round: neither was shot, so 'open a kid's wish list' could only be judged from Home's links.

scores.why: Yardstick. The layout is familiar, but on Home 43 of 56 targets are under 44px, the smallest text is 11.5px, To do shows ISO dates ('Due 2026-09-27') and hides edit/complete behind a disclosure on each card, and nothing on To do marks what is late.

Yardstick. The flows are clear: a NOW line on To do, one-click kind keys on Ideas, To do's Show keys and a meter on Status. But Tab reaches 'Silver Falls hike' and '4 plans on the radar' before the box, and the title 'What's on your mind?' does not say what the app is for.

Legible and calm: 12-13px minimum text and clear lists, with a due-queue rail and NOW line on To do. Home's Fig. 1, a scatter of #ids on a grid under a four-item legend, takes study and does not line up with the rows, and Coming up leaves out the next plan.

The most readable page in the heat: text is 13-15px minimum, each rail stop sits level with its row, and To do's NOW line splits late from coming, so 'what is overdue' reads at a glance. On the phone, '4 more plans / 4 to do / 2 late' are real buttons. Costs: Status lights 'This page' green while Settings says it needs a look, To do's Show is still a select plus a Filter press, and the chat's 950px dotted leaders cross the thread.

The Plans ring ('Next in 1 day') and the folded past weeks help you take in the month at a glance. The pencil-hatched kind squares are harder to tell apart than solid ones, the numbered margin arrows clutter the chat on a phone, and Status's head gives the 30-day spend where the family wants today's.
Keeps t1's hard-to-read Home figure. The countdown screen on Plans ('Next in 1 day, Silver Falls hike') is useful, but the small tubes inside the drawings ('#2', '04') are marks to decode, not words.

The crew board, To do's Show keys and the meter work. But the zero-padded rail (05, 04, 02) takes seven Tab stops before the box, the phone opens on the rail and tube with the box a third of the way down and an icon-only Send, and the ladder bars in Coming up carry no label.

Status is the clearest in the heat: each lamp carries its word ('Working', 'Off', 'Needs a look'), and the rail has plain numbers and sits below the box. Setup marks 'Next'. The crew board still uses '#4 #1' ids to map to rows, Search comes fourth on Ideas, and the lowest text contrast is 4.52.

The master caution band tells a first-time admin exactly what to do next, the same way on Home, Status and Settings ('Choose your own password… then Telegram, then Google Calendar'). Status labels every lamp in words, Home fits in one screen, the rail's 'Late 2' goes to the late rows, and Plans folds its empty past weeks. The arc labels ('3 days', a gap) contradict the rows ('in 4 days'), Send is icon-only on the phone, and the Settings caution's step is not a link.

Its parent's faults plus slower reading: small-caps labels ('SEARCH', 'KIND', 'BOOK THIS FAR AHEAD') are about 8.7px tall, and the slashed-zero padding makes '05' and '01' louder. The rail still comes before the box in Tab order.

Every page is one click from Home, the Ideas kind keys and table make 'only restaurants' one press, and To do has Show keys. But the bar reads 'Home 100', 'Ideas 300', three links come before the box in Tab order, and the settings codes (991-999) are noise to learn to ignore.

The box is first on the glass on every width, with To do beside it on desktop, and the rest of the service is one contents cell. Chat's composer is docked at the foot of the thread, Settings puts what needs a look first, and Ideas keeps the one-click kind keys. The 200/300/400 codes remain, the leaders are nearly invisible on a dim phone, and the month's cells are too short to show more than a clipped plan title.

The most efficient desktop Home: setup is one line with its next step linked, plan rows are led by big day numerals, 'Continue with Vera' leads to the chat, and every page sits on one screen. On the phone the radar and date come before the title so the box drops to mid-screen, the Ideas kind keys scroll sideways with only three showing, and the radar's numerals are 12-16px.

The same flows as t1. The redrawn tab icons give the phone a clearer 'you are here'. The Status meter's square-root scale ('.20' a third of the way along) is easy to misread, and nothing explains the ring segments.

fixes.suggestion: KEEP: the master caution band as the one notice component on Home, Status and Settings; plain-word lamps on Status; the crew board on To do; To do's one-click Show keys (Open/Done/Called off/All); the box before the rail in Tab order; folded past weeks on Plans. FIX: (1) Coming up and Plans: the arcs are labelled with gaps ('3 days' over stop 1) while the row says 'in 4 days'. A tired reader takes them as the same measure, so label each stop with the same 'in N days' as its row, or write gaps as '+3 d' in a dimmer weight. (2) Settings caution: make its bold next step a link, as it is on Home and Status, so the one component behaves one way. (3) Phone: Send is icon-only. Put 'Send where I am' on its own row and give Send its word. (4) The rail's 'Today' cell should not be a link: it goes nowhere useful and costs a Tab stop. (5) The lowest text contrast is 4.64: lift the dim meta text (dates, 'for anyone', the Google note) to at least 5.5 for night use on a phone. (6) The kids' wishes line: make each kid's name a 44px target, not an inline word.

KEEP: the rail with each day and stop level with its row; the NOW line across To do, dividing late from coming; the phone's '4 more plans / 4 to do / 2 late' buttons; the 13-15px minimum type and bone-on-green-black contrast; the title. FIX: (1) Status: 'This page' shows a green lamp while Settings says Sign-in needs a look. Make it the amber 'Partly' lamp, and put the word beside every lamp (console-refine's 'Working / Off / Needs a look'). (2) Home: 'Finish setting up' takes four rows. Graft the one-line caution: 'Next: Choose your own password → then Telegram, then Google Calendar'. (3) To do: replace the Show select plus Filter button with segmented keys that act in one press. (4) Chat: stop the dotted leaders at the bubble's edge, or drop them over about 46rem, so they stop reading as ruled lines through the thread. (5) Plans month: the week rail repeats the grid's rows, so fold the week range into the grid's first column and let the NOW line run in the grid alone. (6) '2 late' should open To do filtered to late, distinct from 'All 4'. (7) Drop the '#1'-'#4' ids from Home's Lately added: they are for the machine, not the family. (8) Sign-in sits hard left on a wide screen; put the field where the eye lands (centred, or on the page's main column).

b.titles: Best: 'Tell Vera what to plan.' (the whole Figure lineage). It is an invitation, says who hears you, and says the job in one verb that covers weekends, ideas, the calendar and reminders. It fits one phone line, and the lit word lands at the end where the eye stops. A close second: 'What's the plan?' (console-refine, all the switchboards). It is the family's own kitchen-table phrase, short and warm. It does not name Vera, but her name sits just above it on every design that uses it. 'What are we planning?' (console-graft) is inclusive, but the -ing reads as a question about plans already made, so it invites a reminder or a someday idea less clearly, and it is longer. 'Anything to plan?' (switchboard-graft) is friendly, but it reads as a yes/no question ('no'), and at the tube's middle strength 'Anything to' is dimmer than the rest of the page's heads. 'Tell Vera what's next.' (console-mut, a dice mutant keeping its parent's words) fails: ideas kept for someday and the kids' wish lists are not 'next', and 'next' competes with the NEXT UP tube beside it. b.titles: Best: 'Tell Vera what to plan.' (Figure Ground) and 'What are we planning?' (Master Caution). 'Tell Vera what to plan.' names who hears you and says the job in one verb, and the lit word sits at the line's end where the eye stops. It is the manual's own voice. A skeptic notes it is an order rather than a question, and the period makes it a touch curt, but it is the clearest about the job. 'What are we planning?' puts the family and Vera in one household 'we' and is an ongoing, open invitation that covers ideas kept for someday as well as dated plans, though 'planning' is a long word to light. 'What's the plan?' (Lamps and Legs, Switchboard Settled and Metered) is warm and short, but it assumes a plan already exists: it asks you to report one more than to hand Vera a reminder or a wish, and it does not name her. 'Anything to plan?' (Switchboard Patched) suits an operator's open line on the glass, but 'anything' makes the question sound like a waiter asking. 'Tell Vera what's next.' (Ladders, Reset, and Lamps and Ladders) fails: it is too narrow (ideas for someday and wish lists are not 'next') and it collides with the NEXT UP tube beside it. 'What's on your mind?' (today, Desk Terminal) fails as a generic chatbot prompt.
